messages:
maria: Posting the initial PRD + RFC draft for the adaptive attention kernel + KV-cache policy changes. High level: reduce tail latency for long-context chats, add deterministic fallback when quantized kernels miss accuracy, and a per-tenant KV eviction override. Link: https://rwd.internal/notes/PRD-2140001234 :eyes:

devon: skimmed. nice framing. can we call out exact perf targets? we need numbers for sprint planning.

carl: agree with devon. propose targets: p95 <= 120ms for 2k seq host models, p99 <= 350ms for 8k seq; token cost delta <= +8% compared to current baseline; correctness < 1% regressions on our eval set.

emily: also add rollout gates: canary at 1% traffic, monitor next-token perplexity (windowed) + user-facing error rate. auto-rollback if user error rate > 0.5% or latency > 2x baseline for 10m.

anu: edge cases to enumerate in RFC: mixed-precision kernels fallback when KV hits are cold, multi-shard attention ordering, and failure mode for KV eviction on low-memory nodes. include small repro snippets.

maria: yes. I'll add an "edge cases" section. for acceptance criteria I was thinking: (1) perf targets (carl's numbers) (2) no more than 1 production incident attributable to new kernel in first 2 weeks of rollout (3) deterministic fallback behavior documented + unit tests (4) migration plan for Dedicated customers.

devon: customer asks: two large customers asked for ability to pin aggressive eviction policy per-tenant for cost control. RFC should include API surface: PATCH /v1/models/:id/kv_policy {"eviction_priority": "aggressive|balanced|conservative"}.

carl: note: that API needs auth + audit log. product will want audit events for any per-tenant override. add to acceptance criteria.

emily: validation checklist for release: e2e perf harness results, regression eval on our 8k prompts suite, chaos test for partial KV loss, canary dashboard with these metrics wired: latency_p95, perplexity_delta, inference_error_rate, tenant_eviction_hits.

anu: small impl note: when fallback happens we should emit a span/log with kernel_variant and kv_hit_flag so Console can correlate. otherwise we blind-spot fallbacks.

ops-bot: deploy check: next deploy window Wed 10:00 UTC. required approvals: eng-runtime lead, product manager, security signoff.

maria: timeline proposal: draft RFC -> review this week, address comments -> lock acceptance criteria by Fri -> cut implementation sprint starting Mon. can we commit owners? devon (tech lead), maria (product lead), carl (runtime QA), emily (observability), anu (kernel implementer).

devon: I can lead. initial PR will include a compatibility matrix for quantized kernel variants and expected perf curves.

carl: I'll author the QA plan and test cases. want to include regression thresholds and exact datasets.

emily: I'll add dashboards and alerting runbook snippets. recommend an SLO burn window of 2 hours for human review before auto-rollback.

anu: question on scope negotiation: do we need the per-tenant API in the first rollout? shipping kernel + KV behavior without tenant overrides is much simpler.

maria: good call. suggest we split into phases: Phase A: kernel + deterministic fallback + observability + rollout gates. Phase B: per-tenant eviction API and Dedicated migration. Phase A must meet acceptance criteria before Phase B. I'll update PRD accordingly.

devon: +1 to phased approach. keeps launch risk smaller.

emily: can we add a monitoring spike to verify observability hooks before enabling canary? 1-day internal spike with synthetic traffic.

maria: done — will add to timeline. planning note: product needs a short customer-facing RFC summary for support and CSMs. I'll draft a 1-pager.

carl: two final edge cases to add: (1) warmup behavior for very large KV ( > 32GB across shards) (2) how we behave when a node returns partial kv reads (merge semantics).

anu: will draft failure-mode tests for both.

maria: thanks all. please comment on the doc by EOD. I'll iterate and tag approvals once updated. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: add security review by @security-team before Friday to avoid blocking Wed deploy window.
